abstract: We study zero-shot fine-grained singing technique conversion (STC), which applies specified techniques to selected regions of an existing singing recording while preserving lyrics, melody, timing, and singer identity. Existing singing conversion and synthesis methods offer complementary strengths in source preservation and explicit technique control, but combining both in an audio-to-audio setting remains underexplored, especially with limited technique-annotated data. We propose ProSing, a zero-shot fine-grained STC framework that adapts a pretrained flow-matching acoustic model with frame-level technique conditioning. To mitigate conditioning shortcuts during adaptation, we introduce a paired training strategy to learn generalizable technique representations. We further incorporate continuous pitch trajectories for explicit and expressive control of pitch-related techniques. Subjective and objective evaluations on unseen singers and source recordings show that ProSing achieves accurate technique control while preserving singing naturalness and singer similarity.
